renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: ss_sequence_track
  title: Predicted state along the sequence
  description: |-
    Each cell is a residue of the protein, coloured by its predicted state (helix, strand or coil), with a lane below for the probability of that state. It answers which stretches fold into which structure and how sure the model is.
    How to read: long helix or strand runs with high confidence are likely real elements. Short stretches with low confidence are uncertain and may flip with a small change in the sequence. Compare the track with domain and structure tiles of the same protein.
    Note: S4PRED predicts from the single sequence, with no alignment.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/psipred/s4pred/main/README.md
  kind: sequence_track
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    residue: residue
    category: category
    value: value

- component: advanced_viz
  id: ss_ribbon
  title: Secondary structure ribbon
  description: |-
    The ribbon draws the predicted structure of the protein as helices, strand arrows and coil, shaded by how confident the prediction is, with the three state probabilities beneath it. It answers where the structural elements are and where the call is ambiguous.
    How to read: dark, clear helices and strands are confident calls. Pale stretches, or places where the helix and strand probabilities are close, are ambiguous. The segment list gives the span of each element for follow-up.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/psipred/s4pred/main/README.md
  kind: secondary_structure
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    residue: residue
    state: ss_code
    p_helix: p_helix
    p_strand: p_strand
    p_coil: p_coil

- component: card
  id: ss_confidence
  title: Prediction confidence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median probability S4PRED gives to the state it called at each residue, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how confident the model is over the whole protein.
    How to read: values close to one mean most residues are called with certainty. Lower values point to disordered or ambiguous regions, where the predicted state should not be trusted.
  column: value
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: probability of the called state, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: ss_residues
  title: Residues by state
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of residues predicted, with the longest protein length beside it, and the bars rank the states by how many residues take them. It answers the helix, strand and coil composition.
    How to read: a protein rich in helix or strand is mostly structured, while a coil-dominated one is probably flexible or disordered. Filter to one protein to see its own composition.
  column: position
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: category
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: residues, by predicted state

- component: figure
  title: Confidence by predicted state
  description: |-
    Each bar counts residues in a probability bin, split by predicted state. It answers which states the model calls with confidence.
    How to read: a state whose residues pile up near one is called reliably. A state spread toward lower values, often coil or strand, is called with more doubt.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: value
    color: category
    barmode: overlay
    labels:
      value: Probability of the predicted state
      category: Predicted state

- component: table
  title: Residue predictions
  description: |-
    Each row is a residue with its position, amino acid, predicted state, the probability of that state and the three state probabilities. It answers what the model predicted at each position.
    How to read: filter to one protein and sort by position to read the sequence, or sort by confidence to find the uncertain residues.
